question: do we still use github.com/lib/pq?

Hi! Can you tell me in which stable version this commit is planned to be included https://github.com/knadh/listmonk/commit/7bfbd6a856123ebd2bb067f9195c3e29660dc764
Also Is it possible to correctly delete all subscribers bypassing the web interface? How to do it correctly in the psql console?
Thank you!

Dependencies: Postgres uses the existing `lib/pq`. MySQL adds `go-sql-driver/mysql` (pure Go, small). MongoDB adds the official driver, which is heavier, so I'd propose SQL sources first and MongoDB as a follow-up PR if this is accepted.
UI: given #3073, the first PR would be backend and API only. The admin screens (list sources, test connection, field mapping, run now, last result) would come after v7 on the new server-rendered admin UI.
**Additional context**
I have a working prototype of this against an older listmonk version and would port it to current `master` in small PRs. Before doing that, is this something you'd consider for core, or would you prefer it stays a separate sidecar project?

Please just stop adding `-beta` to the actual Git tags and use the parse-able semantic `vX.Y.Z` format. Feel free to add "Beta" to the release **titles** on Github, just not the actual git tag. It can also be embedded as part of the BUILDSTR for now, and the Github releases can be left in "pre-release" mode to indicate they are not expected to be stable releases, but please make it easier on actual programming by not making the version tags so hard to parse.
